QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_55

question.text: Using the same Kalpataru data (Committed capital INR 50 cr, NAV Y3 INR 70 cr, hurdle 10% p.a., incentive fee 20%), BUT with a 100% CATCH-UP clause — amount distributed to the MANAGER:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Example 9.4 (100% catch-up): Total profit INR 20 cr; hurdle INR 16.55 cr; residual INR 3.45 cr. Manager's target total profit share = 20% × 20 = INR 4 cr. With a 100% catch-up, the entire residual goes to the manager until the target is met. Since the residual of INR 3.45 cr is insufficient to reach the INR 4 cr target, all INR 3.45 cr is distributed to the manager. The Trap: Option A (INR 0.69 crore) is the NO-catch-up outcome. Option C (INR 4.00 crore) is the manager's full target share, which is unreachable here. Option B (INR 20.00 crore) is the total profit, not the manager's share. Note: The same fund performance can yield very different manager outcomes depending on whether the waterfall includes a catch-up provision.
